documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual exam, 59 yo.
Interval: fully vaccinated for COVID in March. Energy 'better than the fall but not what it was.' Rheum saw her in April, no changes. Walking again daily. Sleeping ok.
Meds: MTX 20 mg weekly, folic acid 1 mg, prednisone 5 mg, ibuprofen prn (less often), calcium 600 BID, D3 2000 IU, lisinopril 10 mg.
Allergies: sulfa, latex.
Screens: PHQ-2 negative. No falls.
Exam: BP at goal. HEENT normal. Thyroid normal. Heart RRR no murmur. Lungs clear. Breasts without masses, axillae clear. Abdomen soft, no HSM. Joints without synovitis. Skin intact, no rashes. Mildly pale.
A/P:
- Health maintenance: mammogram ordered. Colonoscopy due 2027. Pap/HPV next 2023. Shingrix #1 today (recombinant, fine on her meds), #2 in 2 months.
- HTN controlled, lisinopril.
- RA/MTX: labs today.
- Anemia of chronic disease, following.
- Osteoporosis: calcium/D, continue.
RTC 6 months.

reports.text: Bilateral CC and MLO views. Scattered areas of fibroglandular density. No mass, suspicious calcifications or distortion. Stable from March 2019.

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Noticed a lump behind the R knee about a week ago when sitting cross-legged. Not painful. Maybe an ache at the end of a long walk. No fall or twist. No calf pain, no leg swelling.
Exam: soft fullness in the R popliteal fossa, nontender. No erythema or warmth. Calf soft, nontender, no asymmetry. Knee without effusion, ROM full.
Impression: likely popliteal cyst given RA; want it looked at properly and a clot excluded. Referred to orthopedics - she prefers the group that did her left knee; they can image there. Call right away if calf pain or sudden swelling.
Flu vaccine today.

conditions.label: Synovial cyst of popliteal space [Baker], right knee

reports.text: Right lower extremity. Common femoral, femoral, popliteal and posterior tibial veins compressible with normal phasic flow and augmentation. No intraluminal thrombus. In the popliteal fossa there is a well-defined cystic structure with a neck that communicates with the knee joint.
reports.conclusion: No right lower extremity DVT. Popliteal (Baker's) cyst communicating with the knee joint.

documents.title: Venous Duplex Report
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Faxed ultrasound report from the outside orthopedics office, study dated 10/18/2021. No clinic note attached. Routed to PCP.

documents.title: Outside Report Reviewed
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: No DVT. Baker's cyst R knee. Added to problem list. Asked front desk to request the ortho note.

documents.title: Knee visit
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, just letting you know how the orthopedic visit went Monday. The surgeon felt a soft lump about 4 cm behind my knee and said it isn't tender or warm and light doesn't shine through it. My knee bends fine, just a little twinge when I bend it all the way. The ultrasound showed no clot and that it is a cyst connected to the joint. He said to leave it alone and come back only if it gets bigger or starts to hurt. No draining it for now. I've had it about three weeks.

documents.title: RE: Knee visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Thanks, Diane, that matches the report we got. Watching it makes sense. If your calf ever gets suddenly swollen or painful, call us the same day.

Turned 60 last month. Feeling decent. Baker's cyst still there, not bothering her. RA quiet per rheum in March.
Meds and allergies unchanged (sulfa, latex).
PHQ-2: 1.
Exam: BP fine. Heart, lungs normal. Abdomen benign, no organomegaly. R popliteal fullness, soft, nontender. No synovitis. No edema.
Plan: PCV20 today given immunosuppression. Mammogram ordered. Labs. Continue lisinopril, calcium/D. RTC fall.

documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Follow-up, rebooked from November.
Feels about the same, some fatigue that she attributes to the short days. No new joint swelling. Cyst behind R knee unchanged.
Home BP 120s-130s/70s-80s.
Exam: BP acceptable. Heart and lungs normal. Abdomen soft, nontender. No synovitis.
Labs this morning back during visit: Hgb in the usual range, chemistries normal.
A/P: HTN at goal - lisinopril 10. RA quiet on MTX/pred per rheum. Anemia of chronic disease unchanged. Physical in late spring.
